state.paragraph: On December 13, 2014, the board met in person, together with the members of management and representatives of J.P. Morgan and Wachtell Lipton, to discuss and review the final bids and to consider the proposed transaction. Representatives of J.P. Morgan reviewed the respective bids as well as the recent progression of the sale process. Representatives of Wachtell Lipton reviewed the terms of the draft merger agreement and other transaction documents and reviewed the financing commitments that had been provided by the Buyer Group. Representatives of J.P. Morgan made a financial presentation concerning the proposed transaction with the Buyer Group, as well as the Company's alternatives to a sale of the Company, including a leveraged share repurchase. J.P. Morgan then rendered its oral opinion, which was subsequently confirmed in writing, to the board that, as of that date, and based upon and subject to the factors, assumptions and limitations set forth in its opinion, the merger consideration of $83.00 in cash to be paid to the holders of the Company's common stock in the merger was fair, from a financial point of view, to such holders. Following extensive discussion, the board unanimously determined that the merger agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the merger, were advisable and in the best interests of PetSmart and its stockholders, and to recommend that the Company's stockholders approve the adoption of the merger agreement. The board's determination was subject, however, to confirmation that the remaining open points in the merger agreement had been satisfactorily resolved, and the board determined to reconvene, if deemed necessary by the ad hoc committee or the chairman of the board.

ledger_rows.Note: Final-bid deadline reached; the target received two written final bids and Bidder 3’s verbal indication.
Final cash bid with revised transaction documents; committed financing had been provided on 12/06; documentation was less conditional than Bidder 2’s.
Final cash bid with a revised merger agreement; its documentation was comparatively more conditional than Buyer Group’s.
Verbal whole-company indication; ceiling was approximately the current stock price, not a written final offer.
J.P. Morgan said the valuation was unlikely to compete; Bidder 3 then did not submit the requested written offer. Attribution is flagged.
Required the two remaining bidders to improve by 12/12; treated as an extension within the already announced final round.
Approved Buyer Group’s request to work with Longview; they formed a rollover-support relationship but not a separate bidding group.
Improved-bid deadline; Bidder 2 and Buyer Group submitted revised bids that evening.
Submitted revised agreements and financing commitments; later confirmed $81.50 was best and final.
Oral revision; said it was working to increase the offer within hours. Revised agreements and financing commitments accompanied the final sequence.
Best and final cash offer; revised documents were, with few exceptions, substantially executable and financing commitments were supplied.
Selected Buyer Group and approved its merger, subject to satisfactory resolution of remaining agreement points.
Buyer Group’s $83 offer was selected over Bidder 2’s standing $81.50 best-and-final offer.
$83.00 per share in cash; Longview voting agreement and related transaction agreements also executed.
Issued a press release announcing the signed transaction.

adviser.instructions: `paragraph` reports that a financial or legal adviser is retained, engaged, terminated or first shown acting for the target, a committee or a bidder. Is every such event in `paragraph` recorded by some entry in `ledger_rows` (same party, same kind of event, consistent date)?

criteria.true: Each such event has a matching ledger entry, possibly summarised in an entry's Note.
criteria.false: At least one such event in the paragraph has no matching ledger entry.
